title: U.S. House · Michigan's 6th District
area: Michigan's 6th Congressional District — Ann Arbor, Ypsilanti, and downriver Detroit suburbs in Washtenaw and Wayne counties.

context.text: Cook Political Report rated Michigan's 6th District D+12 for the 2026 cycle. Kamala Harris won the district 60.4%–37.1% in 2024.
Incumbent Debbie Dingell was unopposed in the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary. Heather Smiley was unopposed in the Republican primary.

candidates.name: Debbie Dingell
candidates.ballotNote: Unopposed in the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary

summary.text: Dingell is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Michigan's 6th District, first elected in 2014. Before Congress she spent more than 30 years at General Motors, including as president of the GM Foundation.

background.text: Born in Detroit, Michigan, in 1953; earned a bachelor's degree in foreign service from Georgetown University (1975) and a master's degree in liberal studies (1996).

Worked for General Motors for over 30 years, including as president of the GM Foundation and as a senior executive handling public affairs; also chaired the Manufacturing Initiative at the American Automotive Policy Council.
Served on the Wayne State University Board of Governors from 2007 to 2014.

priorities.text: Every American has a right to quality healthcare. Plain and simple.
The time to act on climate change is now and strong US leadership on the world's stage is needed.
Inaction is not an option, and solutions to protect Americans deserve thoughtful debate and consideration. Everyone should be able to live in their communities without fear.

positions.summary: Supports H.R. 8, the Bipartisan Background Checks Act, and has led bipartisan bills such as the Zero Tolerance for Domestic Abusers Act and the Jake Laird Act (national red flag legislation).
positions.quote: I am proud to support H.R. 8, the Bipartisan Background Checks Act of 2019. This landmark legislation would require a background check for every firearm purchase, closing loopholes that have allowed domestic abusers and severely mentally ill individuals to obtain dangerous, military-style weapons and use them to commit gun violence.

positions.summary: Says healthcare is a right, not a privilege, and says she has led the fight for Medicare for All in Congress while supporting legislation to let Medicare negotiate drug prices.
positions.quote: I've been proud to lead the fight for Medicare for All in Congress, and we've made incredible progress so far.

positions.summary: Calls climate change an urgent, existential threat and has introduced the 100% Clean Economy Act to move the country to net-zero carbon emissions by 2050 and legislation to speed the transition to electric vehicles.
positions.quote: This begins by ensuring America honors its commitments under the Paris Agreement and followed up by taking bold actions to reduce man-made greenhouse gas emissions to zero—this includes shifting our economy to one run on renewable energy sources

positions.summary: After the Dobbs ruling, called reproductive care health care and said she would demand that abortion rights be enshrined in law.
positions.quote: You will find me with a movement united at the Supreme Court and all over Michigan demanding these rights be enshrined in our laws.

positions.summary: Says across-the-board tariffs risk harming workers and companies, while describing tariffs as a tool that can be used strategically.
positions.quote: Across-the-board tariffs risk harming the very workers and companies we seek to protect, disrupting integrated supply chains, and pushing investment offshore.

positions.summary: Says raising the federal minimum wage is the easiest way to help working families and cites her support for the Raise the Wage Act, which would increase it to $15.
positions.quote: The easiest way we can do this is by raising the minimum wage.

record.text: In the 119th Congress (2025–2026), serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce (Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade; Communications and Technology; Health) and the House Committee on Natural Resources (Energy and Mineral Resources; Water, Wildlife and Fisheries).
Introduced the 100% Clean Economy Act, which would transition the U.S. to a net-zero carbon emissions economy by 2050.
Leads the bipartisan Zero Tolerance for Domestic Abusers Act, which closes loopholes allowing perpetrators of dating violence and misdemeanor stalking convictions to legally access guns.

candidates.name: Heather Smiley
candidates.ballotNote: Unopposed in the August 4, 2026 Republican primary

summary.text: Smiley is a former Ford Motor Company global business leader running as the Republican nominee against incumbent Debbie Dingell.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree (1985) and a master's degree in administration (2001) from Central Michigan University.
Worked at Ford Motor Company from 1990 to 2022, including global leadership roles in data insights and analytics, product and program management, strategy and planning, and supply chain.
